title: "Amos"

# Amos

::: {.book-summary}
## Book Summary Insight

Amos proclaims God's demand for justice, righteousness, and sincere worship. The book teaches that religious activity without obedience is unacceptable to God.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 1

<div class="key-verse">Amos 1:3</div>

<div class="identifier">For three transgressions and for four</div>

### Why This Verse

Repeated prophetic formula

### Chapter Insight

This chapter begins with judgments against Israel's surrounding nations. The key verse emphasizes that God holds all peoples accountable for their actions.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 2

<div class="key-verse">Amos 2:7</div>

<div class="identifier">They pant after the dust of the earth</div>

### Why This Verse

Social injustice condemned

### Chapter Insight

This chapter continues judgments against the nations and turns specifically to Judah and Israel. The key verse highlights Israel's guilt despite receiving God's blessings and revelation.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 3

<div class="key-verse">Amos 3:3</div>

<div class="identifier">Can two walk together, except they be agreed?</div>

### Why This Verse

One of Amos' most quoted verses

### Chapter Insight

This chapter explains why God is judging Israel. The key verse emphasizes that privilege brings responsibility and accountability before God.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 4

<div class="key-verse">Amos 4:12</div>

<div class="identifier">Prepare to meet thy God</div>

### Why This Verse

Famous prophetic warning

### Chapter Insight

This chapter recounts God's repeated attempts to bring Israel to repentance. The key verse reveals that God's discipline was intended to lead His people back to Him.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 5

<div class="key-verse">Amos 5:24</div>

<div class="identifier">Let judgment run down as waters</div>

### Why This Verse

One of the most cited justice passages in Scripture

### Chapter Insight

This chapter calls Israel to seek the Lord and live. The key verse emphasizes genuine righteousness rather than empty religious observance.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 6

<div class="key-verse">Amos 6:1</div>

<div class="identifier">Woe to them that are at ease in Zion</div>

### Why This Verse

Warning against complacency

### Chapter Insight

This chapter condemns complacency and self-indulgence. The key verse warns against false security amid spiritual decline.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 7

<div class="key-verse">Amos 7:8</div>

<div class="identifier">A plumb line in the midst of My people</div>

### Why This Verse

Famous prophetic image

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records visions of coming judgment and Amos's confrontation with Amaziah. The key verse highlights the prophet's faithfulness in delivering God's message.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 8

<div class="key-verse">Amos 8:11</div>

<div class="identifier">A famine of hearing the words of the LORD</div>

### Why This Verse

Frequently quoted verse

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains the vision of the basket of summer fruit. The key verse warns of a coming famine of hearing God's word.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 9

<div class="key-verse">Amos 9:11</div>

<div class="identifier">I will raise up the tabernacle of David</div>

### Why This Verse

Quoted in Acts 15

### Chapter Insight

This chapter concludes with judgment followed by restoration. The key verse promises the future rebuilding and blessing of God's people.
:::
